# Yes, packages will be deleted

When you run `pyenv virtualenv-delete <venv-name>`, **everything** in that virtual environment gets deleted, including:

- ✅ All installed packages (pip packages)
- ✅ The Python interpreter copy
- ✅ Any configuration files in the venv
- ✅ The entire virtual environment directory

## What actually happens

The command removes the entire directory located at:
```
~/.pyenv/versions/<venv-name>/
```

## Quick verification before deleting

```bash
# See what packages are installed in the venv
pyenv activate <venv-name>
pip list
pyenv deactivate
```

## If you want to save the package list first

```bash
# Activate and export requirements
pyenv activate <venv-name>
pip freeze > requirements.txt
pyenv deactivate

# Now safe to delete
pyenv virtualenv-delete <venv-name>
```

This way you can recreate the environment later with `pip install -r requirements.txt`.
